qt: to the Commission César Luena (S&D) Subject:

According to a report published by Oxfam on 16 October 2026 entitled Toxic Trade1, the European Union continues to export to non-EU countries highly hazardous pesticides whose use is banned in the EU because of their health or environmental risks. The report documents their use in countries such as Brazil, Peru, South Africa and Uganda, and warns of their consequences for farm workers, rural communities, pollinators and ecosystems. In its Chemicals Strategy for Sustainability, published in 2020, the Commission committed to preventing the export of hazardous chemicals that are banned in the EU. However, six years on, that practice continues. 1.
What view does the Commission take of the fact that those pesticides continue to be exported despite the commitments made in 2020?
When does it plan to put forward a legislative proposal to prohibit the export of pesticides whose use is banned in the EU for health or environmental reasons?
What action will it take to ensure that European companies do not shift the health and environmental risks that EU legislation seeks to prevent to non-EU countries?
